subject: health
title: Fire Safety and 9-1-1
sayTitle: Fire Safety and nine one one
about: Hot things that burn, matches are for grown-ups, what the smoke alarm means, get out and stay out, stop-drop-roll, and calling 9-1-1 for real emergencies only. NC 1.PCH.2.2 to 1.PCH.2.4; schools teach this around Fire Prevention Week in October.
tip: Pick a family meeting spot outside and practice stop, drop and roll on the carpet so it feels like a game.

cards.q: Which of these can burn you?
cards.note: Stoves, ovens, irons and hot pans get very hot. Stay back from them.

cards.q: Who may use matches and lighters?
cards.note: Only grown-ups. If you find matches or a lighter, leave them alone and tell a grown-up.

cards.q: Where do you stay when someone is cooking?
wrong: right next to the hot pan
cards.note: Stay three big steps away from the stove.

cards.q: What beeps loudly to warn you about smoke?
cards.note: A smoke alarm is loud so it can wake you up.

cards.q: You hear the smoke alarm. What do you do?
cards.note: Get outside first. Do not stop for toys.

cards.q: If you see smoke, how do you move?
cards.note: Smoke rises. Clean air is near the floor.

cards.q: Once you are outside, do you go back in?
cards.note: Get out and stay out. Firefighters go in, not kids.

cards.q: Where does your family meet after getting out?
cards.note: Pick a spot outside, like the mailbox or a big tree.

cards.q: If your clothes ever catch fire, what do you do?
cards.note: Stop where you are. Drop to the ground. Roll over and over.

cards.q: In stop, drop and roll, why do you roll?
cards.note: Rolling on the ground puts the flames out.

cards.q: When you stop, drop and roll, what do you cover?
cards.note: Cover your face with your hands while you roll.

cards.q: What number do you call in an emergency?
cards.note: Say it like this: nine, one, one. A grown-up can help you call.
An emergency means someone needs help right away.

cards.q: Is it okay to call 9-1-1 for fun?
cards.sayQ: Is it okay to call nine one one for fun?
cards.note: The helpers must stay free for people who really need them.

cards.q: What do you tell the 9-1-1 helper?
cards.sayQ: What do you tell the nine one one helper?
cards.a: your name, address and what is wrong
wrong: a funny joke and a song
cards.note: The helper needs to know where to send help.

cards.q: After you tell 9-1-1 what is wrong, what do you do?
cards.sayQ: After you tell nine one one what is wrong, what do you do?
cards.note: Stay on until the 9-1-1 helper says it is okay to hang up.

cards.q: A firefighter in a big mask comes to help. What do you do?
cards.note: Firefighters look big and loud in their gear, but they are helpers.
